unlabelled_terms.clinical_narrative: A 45-year-old male with a history of asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) developed a severe asthma exacerbation. He was prescribed corticosteroids, which led to significant improvement in his symptoms.

A 60-year-old female with hypertension and diabetes mellitus was prescribed antihypertensive medications. She experienced dizziness and lightheadedness, which resolved after adjusting her medication regimen.
A 55-year-old male with arthritis was prescribed NSAIDs for pain management. He developed gastrointestinal bleeding, necessitating a switch to a proton pump inhibitor.
A 35-year-old female with schizophrenia was prescribed antipsychotics. She experienced extrapyramidal symptoms, including tremors and dystonia, which were managed with a dose adjustment.
A 70-year-old male with atrial fibrillation was prescribed anticoagulants. He developed a minor skin bruise, which was attributed to the anticoagulant therapy.
